text: The Buddhist doctrine of anatta (no-self) claims that:
choices: there is a permanent, unchanging self underlying the flow of experience
the self is an immaterial soul that survives bodily death
what we call the self is only a conventional designation for a stream of causally connected mental and physical events -- there is no substantial, persisting self
each person is constituted by the narrative they tell about their life
explanation: Anatta analyses the person into the five aggregates (skandhas) and finds no abiding self over and above the causally linked stream -- a view the book links to Hume's bundle theory and Parfit's reductionism. Option 0 is exactly what anatta denies; option 1 is the substance-soul view; option 3 is the narrative account.
